system.summary: Graphic substitution alphabet with a few homophones (a, o, u, n), signs for doubled letters (tt, ss, ff, ll) and two nomenclator signs (King of Hungary, Venetians); the same alphabet as matthias1482.
system.notes: The 1482 alphabet looks different from those of the 1486 letters (RESULT.md); R1142 (March 1486) says it uses the old cipher and encloses a new one. Split 14 Oct 2026: R1142 is beatrice1486, R1143 beatrice1486b, R1154 (not a cipher) beatrice1505. Key rebuilt 14 Nov 2026 from the Vestigia cipher/clear pairs (vestigia/README.md): 17 letter values shared with matthias1482; 9 = d and 2 = g here, against 9 = e and 2 = d/i in the matthias1482 key (open point there; one key by the evidence, the two targets not folded, owner's decision).

tools: Python alignment and Levenshtein scoring (vestigia/train_key.py, measure.py)

solution.what: Extracted five exact dates, recipients and shelfmarks from cached DECODE metadata; web reader could not open live DECODE page.
Used existing user-authorized DECODE cookie to acquire all 18 images. R1143 has repeated photographs with decipherment slips moved.
Located MDE III nos. 10 and 12 for both 1482 letters, III no. 75 for May 1486, IV supplement no. 45 for March cipher and III no. 54 for its closing.

Matched dates, clear wording, cipher boundaries and R1143 manuscript slips to older readings. Rendered print confirms italics and March Virtus/Fortis/M. markers. No exhaustive key verification claimed.
Visual inspection of MDE III p. 17 corrects OCR holla to printed balla. Preserve machine extracts as uncorrected evidence.

Entry split under the one-key rule (Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): the 1482 letters R1140 and R1141 keep this entry; R1142 and R1143 (1486, alphabets that look different, and R1142 announces a new cipher) and the plain letter R1154 have their own entries.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): the OCR extracts of the 1877 printed decipherments (MDE III nos. 10, 12) as decryptions; no glyph transcription of either cipher exists (project work).

Vestigia's period clear copies (1958, 1961) paired with the cipher originals (1957, 1960). Key K_V rebuilt from R1140 only, frozen by SHA-256 after a pre-registration, measured once on the whole of R1141 (648 signs, blind transcription): characters 0.900, precision 0.867, words 0.644, against best 0.290 of 200 keys shuffled within value classes; threshold 0.85 and +0.30 passed. Restores a cipher run of R1141 left out of the 1877 print ('Venetiani da sua offesa'). Same alphabet as matthias1482 (17 shared values, 2 contradictions).

Integration check of PR #620. measure.py re-run with the relabel argument: 0.900 / 0.867 / 0.644, controls best 0.290 (0.891 without the relabelling); hashes of PREREG.md and K_V.json match; own scorer 0.901 against at most 0.346. train_key.py is seeded with 9 = d and 2 = g; re-run without them: 2 = g 10/10, 9 = d 29/33. matthias1482's values on R1141: 9 = e with 2 = d 0.833, with 2 = i 0.843. Vestigia images opened: 62 signs of R1141 agree with the transcription; the margin of the clear copy 1961 has the restored run. Key partial (three shapes without a value, 8 signs, and one unread sign). Order of events by the contributor's record. Guerra 2010 (listed by Vestigia) not opened.

outcome.method_basis: Both letters were already deciphered in print in Magyar Diplomácziai Emlékek III (1877), nos. 10 and 12, with the cipher passages in italics; the prints were matched to the DECODE images (clear wording, dates, cipher boundaries) and no key was applied.
outcome.notes: Matthias's offer of Swiss and cavalry against Venice for money paid at Milan. Split on 14 Oct 2026 from the five-record group. 14 Nov 2026: key rebuilt and validated on a held-out letter; one cipher run of R1141 missing from the 1877 print restored (vestigia/README.md).

texts.label: Pozsony, 31 May 1482
texts.summary: Beatrice of Aragon writes to her sister Eleonora, Duchess of Ferrara, during the War of Ferrara: for 100,000 ducats sent to Milan, King Matthias would raise 16,000 men (10,000 Swiss and 6,000 cavalry) in the Brescia and Verona districts against Venice, but will not declare himself openly before his relations with the league are settled. Decryption: uncorrected OCR of the printed decipherment in Magyar Diplomácziai Emlékek III (1877) no. 10.

texts.label: Pozsony, 8 June 1482
texts.summary: Beatrice reports Matthias's displeasure at the league's unwillingness to spend, repeats the Swiss and cavalry offer, asks for money to be sent to Milan and calls for action rather than negotiations that keep 'returning to the beginning' like a ball game. Decryption: uncorrected OCR of MDE III (1877) no. 12.

reading_review.note: The corrected sentence read against the margin of the period clear copy (Vestigia 1961, image opened): 'et tale che non solamente havia tolto Venetiani da sua offesa ma li haria ridocti a carastia de defenderse'. The rest of the reading is the 1877 print as before; not re-read in full against the copy. The contributor's own review (same date) reported the same correction.
